answer: Cross-epoch action continuity rule requires each identity to present a signed action trace whose hash matches prior epochs; a quill-marked gap breaks the chain and voids continuity. Enforcement checks trace links against an atlas of epoch commitments, and any mismatch forces the identity to pay a per-identity cold-start fee plus full trace re-establishment. Basalt-seeded commitment salts make replay of old traces detectable, so a sybil attacker pays that fee for every identity while also losing all accumulated routing weight.
